b1.note: SAB is gated behind cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP), but the server must also send the correct COEP/COOP headers, and the requirement is not solely the HTTP headers in isolation — the browser must actually process them.

b2.verdict: disagree: timestamp-query (and instant AMD timestamp queries) are not fully exposed to ordinary web content by default in current Chrome as of recent versions; they are exposed under restriction or flag, not unrestricted ordinary content by default
b2.note: The widely used stopwatch query path in WebGPU timestamp queries has been gated or restricted in recent Chrome and is not unconditionally available to any ordinary page by default.

b3.verdict: disagree: WebAssembly threads module validation does not fail solely because cross-origin isolation is absent
b3.note: Threads support (HIR, module-level threads, SharedArrayBuffer) is gated behind the same isolation that SAB needs, but the failure mode is not a simple ‘validation fails’ at module load; it is tied to SAB availability / COOP/COEP, not a runtime validation error in current Chrome.
